title: Structured Output & Function Calling Demo - SummitPay
summary: Redwood AE and SE demoed structured output (JSON mode) and function/tool calling via the API and Console. Customer (SummitPay) is evaluating guardrails, schema enforcement, and secure private deployment for PCI-adjacent payment flows. Key asks: sample pricing for Dedicated, security docs (SOC2/KMS/SAML), and a short pilot with latency/throughput benchmarks. Next steps agreed: send pricing + benchmark template, schedule POC kickoff, share security whitepaper.
topics: Structured JSON mode and schema enforcement
Guardrails and validation - Redwood Optimize suggestions
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/HSM/KMS) for PCI-adjacent data
action_items: Alex Rivera - send Dedicated pricing and pilot T&Cs by 2026-08-20
Priya Desai - share benchmark spreadsheet and sample scripts for latency tests by 2026-08-21
Samir Patel (SummitPay) - provide sample schema + a small dataset for validation by 2026-08-24
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack (SOC 2, ISO overview, KMS/HSM integration docs)
Schedule POC kickoff w/ infra team (proposed week of 2026-08-24)
Customer to confirm pilot scope (throughput targets, success criteria)
transcript:
00:00 Alex Rivera: Hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex on the Redwood team, I'm the account lead. We also have Priya, our solutions engineer. Can you hear us all okay?
00:06 Jordan Lee: Yup sounds good. Jordan here. Thanks for setting this up.
00:10 Alex Rivera: Great. So today we're gonna run through structured output - JSON mode - function calling and how that integrates with the Console and Optimize suggestions. High level is this will show you how to get strict schemas back from the model and how to call your internal order service safely.
00:25 Lisa Gomez: Awesome. Our product folks are particularly interested in making sure the responses follow schema strictly; we had issues with downstream parsers failing when the model returned extra fields.
00:35 Priya Desai: Totally, we see that a lot. We'll demonstrate the schema enforcement options and the runtime guardrails. Quick note: there's a few different enforcement levers: soft validation (warnings), hard validation (reject), and auto-correction heuristics. We'll show all three.
00:50 Samir Patel: Quick question on security: if we do function calling to an internal order API, how do you prevent sensitive tokens from leaking in logs? We also have KMS and HSM requirements for key management.
01:05 Priya Desai: Great question. For hosted setups we mask tokens and we can redact certain fields from audit logs. For Dedicated and Private we integrate with your KMS and HSM for key wrapping and customer-managed keys. Logs can be routed to your SIEM and we support configurable retention.
01:20 Jordan Lee: Is SAML SSO and RBAC supported today for the Console? We need role separation for product and infrastructure teams.
01:26 Alex Rivera: Yes, SAML SSO is supported plus SCIM and you can tie roles in the Console. We'll include the RBAC doc in the security pack.
01:35 Priya Desai: Alright jumping into the demo. I'm switching to the Console view — loading the API playground. First the simple structured output example: we pass a schema that looks like an order object with fields: order_id, items (array), total_cents, currency, and flags like requires_review.
01:55 Priya Desai: (typing) Here's the schema. You'll notice we can set type constraints and enumerations for currency, we also have nested schemas for items. Now I'm going to toggle "strict mode" which enforces shape at runtime and returns an error if the model doesn't match.
02:15 Lisa Gomez: If strict mode errors, do you return a helpful error message with hints? Or do we just get a raw mismatch?
02:22 Priya Desai: We surface a structured error with the path that failed plus a confidence score and a suggested correction if it's a minor deviation. For bigger mismatches we recommend running auto-correct heuristics in a canary first.
02:35 Priya Desai: Now I'll run function calling demo - this is configured so when the model detects an intent to create an order it returns a function call: create_order(order_payload). You can map the payload directly to your internal API contract.
02:49 Priya Desai: (executes) The model returned the function call cleanly. You can see the payload populated as JSON. I'm going to invoke our mock order service and show the round trip.
03:00 Samir Patel: In prod we'd profile latency: what's the expected p50/p95 for a single create_order call if we go Hosted vs Dedicated?
03:09 Alex Rivera: Typical hosted p95 depends on load and model size; for small models we're often sub-300ms p50 and 500-700ms p95 for text-gen flows. For Dedicated you can get tighter SLOs since you have reserved GPUs — p95s in the 200-400ms range are common depending on batch settings and sequence length. We'll send a benchmark template so you can plug in your payload sizes.
03:30 Priya Desai: Also worth mentioning caching: Redwood can do prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts to reduce cost and latency. For structured outputs where schemas are stable, caching is effective.
03:45 Lisa Gomez: How does caching interact with function-calling? We want to ensure idempotency and avoid duplicate order creation.
03:53 Priya Desai: Good point. For any function call flow we recommend using a request-id and server-side dedupe. Redwood's runtime can include the request-id in trace metadata but the dedupe logic lives in your service. The runtime will not re-execute a backend call if the model yields the same function call during retries, but we still advise application-level idempotency keys.
04:12 Jordan Lee: Can you demo a guardrail where the model is prevented from adding extraneous fields like internal_notes?
04:18 Priya Desai: Sure. I'll set a deny-list on fields and toggle the policy to drop unknown fields. (types) Now I'll run the same prompt - the response is stripped of any extra fields and we get a validation warning in the metadata.
04:35 Samir Patel: Nice. Can the system also convert types? For example if total comes back as "$12.00" can it coerce to cents?
04:42 Priya Desai: Yes, there's coercion rules - string to int, currency parsing. We can also run a pre-validation hook to apply transformations. We'll show an example in the API playground docs.
04:55 Alex Rivera: Quick pause: are there any regulatory constraints we should know? Jordan?
05:00 Jordan Lee: We're a payments company, so PCI-adjacent. We cannot send full card numbers to third-party hosts. We prefer either Dedicated or Private with VPC and customer-managed keys. Also need to see logs redaction and audit capabilities.
05:12 Alex Rivera: Understood. We'll include our Private deployment options and how HSM integrates. We'll also include the SOC 2 and penetration test summaries.
05:22 Priya Desai: Back to function calling - I'll switch to the API raw call to show how you'd set the schema in the request body. (reads) You can pass a JSON schema object or use Redwood's simplified schema shorthand. The response JSON comes with a schema_match boolean and a schema_errors array if any.
05:45 Lisa Gomez: Does the Console let non-devs view only the structured payloads? We'd like product to review orders without raw text.
05:51 Alex Rivera: Yes there's a Console view that renders structured outputs in a table and you can apply quick filters. RBAC controls who sees raw prompts vs just the parsed payload.
06:05 Priya Desai: Now I'll demo an end-to-end flow where the model decides to call create_order, returns payload, Redwood runs schema validation, we invoke a mock order service, and Console shows the result with a link to the trace. (executes) You can see the trace shows token-level latency, model variant used, and a cost estimate.
06:30 Samir Patel: About cost: how granular are estimates? We need to tie cost to features.
06:36 Alex Rivera: Token-level and per-route cost breakdowns are available. Optimize will recommend batching or quantization to hit cost targets while monitoring quality metrics. We'll show a sample optimize output in the deck I'll send.
06:50 Jordan Lee: Any concerns around hallucinations in structured output? If the model invents an order_id, do you recommend server-side generation?
06:58 Priya Desai: For critical identifiers we always recommend server-side generation. For fields that can be inferred, schema + strict validation mitigates hallucinations. You can also set deterministic decoding or use a smaller model ensemble for extraction tasks.
07:15 Lisa Gomez: Could you show how function calling integrates with downstream tools, like our ticketing system?
07:21 Priya Desai: Yep - we have a tool calling example where the model can return a payload for create_ticket(ticket_payload). The Console can map that to a webhook or a serverless function. We demo connector templates for common tools.
07:35 Samir Patel: We heard about Redwood Optimize - what's the typical uplift?
07:40 Alex Rivera: It varies. Customers often see 20-50% token cost reduction with batching, cache, and model switching. Optimize also suggests quantized variants for Dedicated to reduce GPU memory and cost.
07:55 Priya Desai: I'm going to intentionally make the model produce a slightly malformed payload so you can see the rejection path. (runs) The runtime returned a 422 with schema_errors: path items[0].quantity expected integer but got "one"; suggested correction: coerce string to int.
08:15 Lisa Gomez: That's helpful. For our legal team we'll need a copy of the audit log retention policy.
08:21 Alex Rivera: We'll include that in the security pack. Also, we'll note options for extended retention as an add-on.
08:30 Jordan Lee: Regarding PII, can we configure redaction to remove e.g., email addresses from transcripts?
08:36 Priya Desai: Yes, you can add redaction rules and we also support streaming redaction at ingestion time.
08:45 Samir Patel: One last infra question: if we run a Private deployment on-prem, does Redwood still manage model updates?
08:52 Alex Rivera: For Private you can opt-in to model updates managed by Redwood or you can pin versions and apply updates via the private control plane. For air-gapped setups we provide an on-prem bundle.
09:05 Priya Desai: Alright wrapping up — recap of next steps. We'll send the pricing and security docs, bench template, and propose a pilot scope.
09:15 Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Let's target next Tuesday for the POC kickoff.
09:20 Alex Rivera: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the links and docs.
09:25 Lisa Gomez: Thanks all.
09:27 Meeting end.
